# URLCode admin

> Operator-installed administration extension for URLCode, on top of the auth
> extension's service: users, sessions, roles, audit, registration approval,
> two-person cases, support impersonation, health. Released with core.
> Apache-2.0.

Install core from npm, then run `npx urlcode init my-site --with ui,auth,admin`, or
`npx urlcode extensions add admin` in an existing site (it adds `auth` and `ui` too).

Part of the URLCode framework, in the same repository: docs/FRAMEWORK.md

## What a project declares (YAML only)
- `extensions.admin: { version: "1", config: {} }`
- A mount: `/admin/*: { extension: admin, methods: [GET, HEAD, POST] }`
- `extensions.ui: { version: "1", config: {} }` declared BEFORE `admin`, with `/assets/ui/*: { extension: ui, methods: [GET, HEAD] }`.
- The operator lists `admin()` after `ui()` and `auth()` in the site's `host.mjs` `composeHost` list
  (options such as `admin({ authMount, sendInvitation, health })`); `composeHost` hands it auth's
  service and CSRF key and the `ui` kit.
- Presentation: screens are `admin/*` kit templates (`adminTemplates`, `adminUiTemplates`) and render
  only through `ui.kit`; admin contributes `adminUiTemplates` to `ui` through `contributes.ui`.
  Activation refuses when `ui` is missing, not yet active, or lacks `adminUiTemplates`. There is no
  second render path.

## Read in this order
- [README](README.md): install, build from reviewed sources, wiring, permissions, console operation, health, exports.
- [SECURITY](SECURITY.md), [threat model](THREAT-MODEL.md).
- [Implementation status](IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md): built and remaining.
- [Acceptance](ACCEPTANCE.md): evidence. The original design spike, clean-project
  test notes and UX review are private maintainer material; this package's
  behavior is documented above, not there.

## Do not guess
- Permissions are auth's names (`auth.users.read`, `auth.users.manage`, `auth.sessions.manage`,
  `auth.audit.read`, `auth.cases.manage`, `auth.users.impersonate`, ...); `*` is full.
  The spike's `admin.*` names do not exist.
- Every write needs a fresh session and a reason; hidden controls are not authorization.
- Impersonation needs service opt-in, its permission and a notification callback, and
  `withSupportBanner` around every application response before it is enabled.
- Role definitions are operator configuration, not console edits.
